nativeSmoke.surface: isolated temporary HOME/profile, documented OpenCode session API, Relay-owned plugin, private Unix-socket bridge
observed: Created disposable empty project-scoped sessions with POST /api/session and verified they had no messages.
The real plugin called session.get for its exact configured session and registered through the bridge.
The plugin read fresh session.wait state idle for the exact configured session.
notObserved: The bridge bind callback was a test callback, not the live Relay supervisor/store.
No session.prompt, provider call, native context observation, turn start, or safe-idle-after-turn was exercised.
Native refusal and restart recovery were not exercised.
cleanup: Both disposable sessions were deleted and read back absent.
The isolated OpenCode server and bridge processes were stopped.

relayAdapterBoundary.invocation: The Relay broker calls startDeliveryAdapter({client, bind, signal, root, onEvidence}) in the broker process; the OpenCode plugin connects over an authenticated private Unix socket.
relayAdapterBoundary.finding: The broker intentionally receives no native SDK/plugin context. The Relay-owned OpenCode plugin runs inside its v2 PluginContext and hands exact session/profile/lifecycle identity plus explicit Relay authority/worker/session/epoch bindings through the private bridge to the existing bind callback. The native smoke used a test bind callback and did not verify live Relay persistence. Other clients remain unimplemented.
relayAdapterBoundary.smallestRequiredAuthorization: OpenCode deployment remains owner-controlled: enable the exported plugin only in an approved isolated profile, grant only explicitly approved native permissions, and supply an explicit existing Relay recipient mapping in plugin options. This stage made no host configuration or permission changes.

runtimeVersions.cursor: Agent CLI 2026.10.01 (WP1); 3.24.12 is a separately observed Cursor component/surface, not the Agent CLI version

clients.surface: Managed hooks and Codex App Server candidate
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: App-server thread resume/turn operations do not establish control of an already-running Codex CLI session. The exact busy, idempotency, refusal, and status path for that session is not established.
clients.smallestNextStep: Provide an owner-approved native bridge to the exact existing CLI session and a supported safe-busy/idempotency/status contract, or an authoritative API proving the same behavior.

clients.surface: Managed hooks and Cursor Agent SDK
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: Cursor Agent CLI 2026.10.01 is the WP1 observed surface; 3.24.12 is a separate Cursor component and must not be conflated with it. The managed hooks are context-only. Agent SDK resume/status is not mapped to the exact running UI/CLI session. Cloud busy rejects rather than queues; local agents do not raise AgentBusyError, and local.force expires a stuck run rather than providing safe busy delivery.
clients.smallestNextStep: Provide an exact-session bridge plus version-matched current status, refusal, safe-boundary, and request-identity semantics for the installed Agent CLI.

clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only

clients.smallestNextStep: Provide the exact runtime version and an authoritative API that safely submits to the same existing idle session and queues at a safe busy boundary.

clients.surface: In-process OMP session API and managed lifecycle extension
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: OMP 18.8.7's public SDK is an in-process embedder, not a verified external attach path to the installed CLI. followUp and session/turn events remain candidates inside the owning runtime; durable request idempotency is undocumented and no Relay consumer is wired.
clients.smallestNextStep: Provide an owner-approved entrypoint inside the exact live OMP session with bounded input/status/event behavior and durable request identity or safe observation/reconciliation semantics.

clients.surface: Kilo v2 session inbox/prompt API candidate
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: The candidate v2 API is not matched to CLI 7.8.8. Replaying the same message ID returns the original admission but schedules another wake unless resume:false, which admits only; sessions.active() is process-local and resets on restart. Backlog/steering bounds, provider timeouts, current status/refusal, and safe busy behavior remain unresolved.
clients.smallestNextStep: Provide a version-matched exact-session API with bounded queue/provider behavior, no unsafe duplicate wake on retry, and current status/refusal/observation semantics.

clients.surface: TaskStart/UserPromptSubmit hook envelope and ClineCore candidate API
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: Hooks can contribute context at their callback boundary. ClineCore send/status/events are in-process APIs not tied to the inspected CLI 3.0.70; safe busy queuing and idempotent retry are unestablished.
clients.smallestNextStep: Provide an owner-approved bridge to the version-matched Cline runtime and verified busy, refusal, status, and idempotency semantics.

clients.surface: Hermes 2026.9.24 in-process Python PluginContext.inject_message on an exact native session key
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: inject_message is callable only inside PluginContext and returns a boolean scheduling result, not an attempt-correlated receipt. Gateway injection requires allow_gateway_injection. The inspected surface lacks caller-keyed idempotency, fresh exact-session status, and correlated context/turn observation; a generic bridge cannot supply these native guarantees. The classic CLI busy path can interrupt and is not suitable for unattended delivery.
clients.smallestNextStep: An explicitly supported native surface must provide caller-keyed idempotent enqueue plus fresh exact-session status and correlated context/turn observation. Any plugin installation or permission grant remains separately owner-authorized.

clients.surface: Managed policy and Zed ACP client
clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: The managed path has no external input consumer for a Zed-owned active session. ACP session/prompt targets the ACP child agent, not the existing Zed-owned assistant session.
clients.smallestNextStep: Provide a Zed-owned input/lifecycle API for the exact already-running assistant session; ACP child launch is not a substitute.

clients.launch: not an adapter capability; existing local Pool/prime only
clients.apiFinding: The packaged plugin implementation checks the configured exact session through PluginContext, uses session.prompt with queue delivery and a stable caller-supplied ID, and separately observes context, model-request, and safe-idle events. Its Relay bindings share one consumer and stable profile/session target gate across local and hub authorities. The v2.0.26 native smoke verified exact session.get, plugin-to-bridge registration, and fresh session.wait idle in an isolated disposable session, but used a test bind callback; no live Relay supervisor/store binding, prompt, provider call, context, turn, or safe-idle-after-turn was observed.
clients.smallestNextStep: In an approved isolated profile, verify the plugin against the live Relay supervisor/store using an explicit existing Relay mapping, then separately qualify native context, turn, safe-idle-after-turn, refusal, and restart recovery without using a real user session or provider spend. Host deployment and permissions remain owner-controlled.
